finalists.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
finalists.why: This candidate has the most diverse and specific set of findings, including a malar rash, bibasilar Velcro crackles, and a grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur, which are all characteristic of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

finalists.label: Infective Endocarditis
finalists.why: Despite the negative blood cultures, the presence of a tricuspid-valve vegetation and a new heart murmur are strong evidence for Infective Endocarditis, making it a strong candidate in this group.

frontier_selector.why: The champion, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, is chosen because it accounts for a broader range of symptoms, including the malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and bibasilar Velcro crackles, which are not fully explained by the runner-up, Infective Endocarditis.
